about.title: About
about.name: Olga Indigo
about.fallback_subtitle: Beninese visual artist specialising in batik, textile art, and natural dyes.
about.intro_text: Born on 1 January 1975 in Bohicon, Benin, Olga Indigo is a visual artist whose work sits at the intersection of painting, textile art, and traditional natural dyeing techniques.
about.intro_text2: Heir to a lineage connected to the ancient Kingdom of Dahomey (1600–1904), she has spent more than thirty years building a body of work rooted in organic pigments, hand-woven Aho cloth, and knowledge passed down within her family.
about.origins_text1: Olga grew up in Bohicon surrounded by the dyers and weavers of her region, watching cloth transform under wax and pigment. Introduced to natural dyes at age 5 by her mother, Marie Rose Lima, she began learning sewing and fabric work at 14.
about.origins_text2: That early apprenticeship — equal parts patience and curiosity — shaped an artistic language rooted in Vodoun ritual, African cosmologies, and the collective memory of the Dahomey feminine heritage.
about.grandma_quote: The cloth never lies. It remembers every hand that touched it, every colour it was asked to carry.
about.grandma_author: Words passed down from her mother, Marie Rose Lima
about.step1_text: Hot wax is applied by hand to the canvas, tracing the lines that will resist the dye and remain untouched by colour.
about.step2_text: The fabric is submerged in natural dye baths, one colour at a time, building depth with every layer the wax protects.
about.step3_text: The wax is melted away to reveal the finished design — a controlled accident where ancestral craft meets contemporary creation.
about.art_text1: Batik is, above all, a dialogue with the unpredictable: cracks in the wax, the way a dye bleeds through hand-woven Aho cloth, the patience a piece demands before it gives up its final form.
about.art_text2: Each canvas Olga creates carries that dialogue forward — a contemporary artwork rooted in a centuries-old West African craft, bearing the symbols and cosmologies of Dahomey.
about.indigo_text: A deep natural blue dye, central to West African textile heritage and the signature tone of Olga Indigo's work since her very beginnings.
about.cola_text: Its husk yields warm reddish-brown tones, traditionally used to enrich and deepen the colour of hand-woven Aho cloth.
about.baobab_text: Bark and pod extracts contribute soft earthy hues, anchoring each piece in the Beninese landscape.
about.teck_text: Crushed teak leaves produce subtle greens and golds, often layered beneath the wax to create a unique natural texture.
about.timeline_title1: FINAB — International Arts Festival of Benin
about.timeline_desc1: Participation in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th editions of FINAB in Cotonou, alongside solo exhibitions at the Institut Français, Hôtel Maison Rouge, and Centre Culturel Le Yes Papa.
about.timeline_desc2: Exhibitions at Galerie Anne de Villepoix (Paris) and Galerie SAGA (Lille) in 2020. In 2019: BISO (Ouagadougou Sculpture Biennale) and FESPACO — 26th edition.
about.timeline_desc3: Based in Sévaré, Mali from 2000 to 2010, exhibiting at the Festival sur le Niger in Ségou (2005–2008). SITA Abidjan (2015), Abidjan Art Festival (2014), SIAO and FESPACO in Ouagadougou (2016–2018).
about.timeline_desc4: At 16, Olga sold her first canvases in Bohicon. She then moved to Cotonou and set up a studio on the Fidjrossè beach — ten years facing the Atlantic that built her clientele and her resolve.
about.representation_text: Olga Indigo is represented by Galerie SAGA (France) — www.galeriesaga.com
about.cta_title: A Question or a Project in Mind?
about.cta_subtitle: Whether it's a custom piece, a commission, or simply curiosity about the work — Olga and her team would love to hear from you.

atelier.title: ATELIER
atelier.our_atelier_desc: Nestled in the heart of Cotonou, the AZIZART atelier is a living space where tradition meets creation. Each piece is born here, from the first wax drawing to the final revelation of colour.
atelier.philosophy_desc: Every gesture is deliberate. Every layer of dye a choice. The atelier is not merely a workshop — it is the crucible where Olga Indigo transforms raw Aho cloth into art that carries memory.

atelier.visit_desc: Olga Indigo opens her atelier by appointment. Contact us to plan your visit.
